about: Every event, condition, action and world effect a world story (Docs/story-programs.md) may use, with typed parameters and a sentence for the Story Creator (Docs/Design/85-story-triggers-and-campaign-control.md, Phase 4). tools/story_program.py reads its tables from here: EVENTS, MISSION_EVENTS, MISSION_MEASURES, EFFECTS and the bounds of every effect parameter. A slot "{a,b,c}" in a sentence is one picker for several keys (a tile: cell, x, y). Version 2 (Phase 5): the conditions and actions marked "v2" need a story of version 2, with declared variables ("variables"); a parameter of type "operand" is a value (a number, a switch, a text, or {"var"}, {"field"}, {"count"}, {"since"}, {"each"}, {"plus"|"minus"|"min"|"max": [a, b]}); an action with "nest" holds lists of actions. Phase 6: quests (a version 2 story's "quests"), audiences "open" and "everyone", and the effects marked "story", which the story keeps itself (quest progress, who takes part, a choice laid over a resident's window) rather than sending to the game; events marked "story" are the story's own facts, sent as it runs and never in the world's log. A parameter marked "optional" may be left out. Phase 8: conditions marked "facts" read the world's facts as of the event (game.story_facts: where a wolf is, what they carry, the time, the weather, standing, a resident's state), and the events marked "watch" are written by the game only while a live story listens for them (its watch list, sent with each phase). Phase 9: more world effects (doc 85, 3.5): telling the wolves, the journal, map markers, trackers, taking items, warrants, strangers, mantles, holds, followers, doors, the ground, boards, the weather (never the calendar), market events, prices, projects, deeds, personal quests and stopping a scene. "actsOnWolves" needs "may act on players' wolves" on a hosted world, "needsBuilder" (factions: relations and standing) a builder or the owner, as approving it does. Phase 10: chapters (story.start, a campaign of stories approved together), "story started" and "story ended" from the story runner, and the events Phase 8 left (a wolf near a resident, a purse or a standing crossing a number the trigger names, a stance changed, mantles, a skill grown, an injury healed): "needsMatch" names the fields a trigger on it must give. "needsBuilder" also marks the effects that change the economy (prices, projects). Doc 86, Phase 1a: the values {"audience": "all|active|online"} (how many wolves the story has; how many were seen in the last activeDays game days, a program field, 18 when not given; how many are signed in now), {"times": [a, b]} and {"div": [a, b]} (floored toward zero; by 0, no value), and the share of the wolves who took part: {"percent": {"list": <a story or world list of wolves>} | {"where": <a test for each wolf>}, "of": "active|all|online"} and {"among": ...} (how many); the condition "participation" (enough of them, with a floor and a cap); a phase's Readiness ("ready": the parts that say it may move on, its exit {"on": "ready"}, auto, then, slowAfterDays, slowNeedsYou, autoAfterDays) and the admin's Advance. A parameter of type "condition" is a condition tree tested once for each wolf, the wolf as $each.

types.wolf: A player's wolf: the acting wolf ($actor) or a named one.
types.town: A town (a region of the map).
types.scene: A scene embedded in this story.
types.cue: A scene cue: the name a scene event comes back with.
types.variable: A declared variable of this story (version 2), of the types the parameter names.
types.operand: A value: a number, on or off, a text, a variable, the event's field, a list's count, a timer's days, the loop's value, a little arithmetic (plus, minus, min, max, times, div), the story's audience counted (all, active, online), or the share (percent) or number (among) of the wolves who took part.
types.whose: Whose value of a variable kept for each wolf or party: the acting wolf's, or the looped wolf's.
types.objective: An objective of the quest named beside it.
types.purse: Who pays: a town's treasury (town:<town>), its works, watch or church (town:<town>:works), a business's till (till:<id>) or a Chapter's treasury (chapter:<id>). Never minted.
types.offer: A story choice's name: what a dialogue choice event comes back with.
types.door: A door of the world (its id: link_<link>_a or _b; a story locks both sides).
types.mantle: A mantle (doc 84): a part a resident takes up, with its own lines.
types.visitor: A temporary resident's id, given by the story (letters, digits, - and _).
types.story: Another story of this world, by its id: a chapter of the same campaign (Phase 10).
types.condition: A condition tree tested once for each wolf, the wolf as $each (doc 86, R1).

once.member: once per wolf in the campaign

exit.players: when {n} different wolves of the story have
exit.ready: when the phase is ready (its Readiness: enough wolves took part, enough days, ...), by itself or when an admin presses Advance

events.title: A directed resident arrives
events.sentence: {actor} arrives at the spot for cue {detail}
events.help: A story's npc.walk order finished: the resident stands on the tile it was sent to.

target.label: the story run the scene belongs to

detail.label: the author's cue on the order

events.notes: tile = the resident's tile on arrival.

events.title: A directed resident speaks
events.help: A story's npc.speak order was carried out: the resident said its line aloud.

target.label: the story run the scene belongs to

detail.label: the author's cue on the order

events.title: A directed resident takes a pose
events.help: A story's npc.pose order finished: the resident is now in the posture asked for.

target.label: the story run the scene belongs to

detail.label: the author's cue on the order

events.title: A directed resident can't do it

target.label: the story run the scene belongs to

detail.label: the author's cue on the order

events.title: A scene finishes
events.help: An embedded scene (cinematic) reached its last beat.

actor.label: the wolf who started the scene, if any

target.label: the story run the scene belongs to

events.title: A scene's choice is made
events.sentence: The choice {detail} is made in the scene

actor.label: the wolf who started the scene, if any

target.label: the story run the scene belongs to

detail.label: cue.option: the scene's cue and the option chosen

events.notes: detail is '<cue>.<option id>'.

events.title: Players answer in a scene
events.help: A response beat of an embedded scene closed, answered by the players or timed out.

actor.label: the wolf who started the scene, if any

target.label: the story run the scene belongs to

events.notes: The typed words are never logged.

events.title: A scene fails
events.help: An embedded scene could not go on (marked failed) and ended.

actor.label: the wolf who started the scene, if any

target.label: the story run the scene belongs to

events.title: A wolf enters a story region
events.help: A wolf's move took it inside a region of a live story that watches regions.

cell.label: the cell of the first tile inside

detail.label: the story run the region belongs to

events.notes: tile = the first tile inside.

events.title: A wolf leaves a story region
events.help: A wolf's move took it outside a region of a live story that watches regions.

cell.label: the cell of the last tile inside

detail.label: the story run the region belongs to

events.notes: tile = the last tile inside.

events.title: Someone talks to someone
events.help: A wolf speaks to a resident (chat or the dialogue window), a resident answers a wolf, or two residents finish an ambient talk.

detail.label: for residents' own talk only: the topic kind (news, deed, friends, day...)

events.notes: Never what was said. Wolf to resident: actor = the wolf. Resident answering: actor = the resident, target = the wolf. actor (or target) is empty for an unrecognised voice. An ambient quarrel is logged as 'quarrel', not this.

events.title: A wolf comes into the world
events.help: A player enters the world with a character (logs in).

events.title: A wolf enters a place
events.help: A wolf crosses a door or a cell edge into another cell or interior (residents' crossings are not logged).
events.notes: detail is a cell or interior id, so a place picker fits it too.

events.title: A wolf leaves the world
events.help: A player's character leaves the world (logs out or disconnects).

events.title: A gift is given
events.help: A character gives goods or coins to another, the first gift of the game day between that pair (the one that warms the bond).

item.label: what was given (empty for coins only)

events.notes: A trigger on 'gift' also fires on 'gift again'. A gift's item filter matches the base item, so a marked or crafted rope counts as rope (unless the filter names marks with ~ or @).

events.title: Another gift the same day
events.help: A character gives to the same receiver again on a game day it has already given to them (no more warmth).

item.label: what was given (empty for coins only)

events.notes: Item filter matches the base item, as for gift.

events.title: Money or goods change hands
events.help: Every move between accounts in the economy's ledger: sales, wages, rent, fees, gifts, prizes, fines, upkeep. Very frequent.

actor.label: the account paying or handing over (a character, or an account such as treasury, stores:<town>, till:<post>, contract:<id>)

cell.label: where the payer is, when it is a character

item.label: the goods moved (empty for coins only)

detail.label: the ledger's reason ('a gift', 'rent', 'stall sale', 'contract reward', 'fine'...)

events.notes: Logged from the society's journal (World::absorbJournal). Accounts are not all characters; tile only when the payer is a character in the world. item may be a marked id (base~marks).

events.title: A contract is fulfilled
events.help: A contract (bounty, escort, courier, supply...) is settled as done: its reward paid to the one who did it, or returned to the poster when nobody took it (the watch cleared the camp, the carters carried it).

actor.label: who did it and was paid (or the poster, when the reward went back)

target.label: what it was for: a bounty's camp, a courier's recipient, an escort's or supply's town

coins.label: what was paid (or the whole reward returned)

events.notes: Written as 'contract ' + status; 'contract expired' is the other status and is not listed. Filter detail by its 'courier:', 'escort:' or 'bounty:' prefix only with exact text.

events.title: An animal is killed in a hunt
events.help: An animal falls in a hunt; its parts go to the hunters.

detail.label: the kill's grade: 'a clean kill', 'a good kill', 'a rough kill' or 'a ragged kill'

quantity.label: kinds of goods taken from it

events.notes: tile = where the animal fell.

events.title: A fight ends
events.help: A battle (a fight or a hunt) is over.
events.notes: No actor or target.

events.title: A Gift is used outside a fight
events.help: A wolf uses a work Gift outside a fight (Mend, Shortcut, Lighten Load, Dowse, Echo, Carry, or lending it to a workshop).
events.notes: item is a Gift family, not an item id. Gifts used in fights are not logged.

events.title: Someone dies
events.help: A character dies: killed in a fight, of old age, or by the Dungeon Master.
events.notes: Old age also records 'old age' straight after.

events.title: Someone is brought back
events.help: A dead character is raised again (a Dungeon Master or developer action).

events.title: Two residents marry
events.help: Once a game week, two unmarried adult residents who like and know each other well enough may marry; one moves in with the other.

events.title: A resident is moved to a new home
events.sentence: {actor} is sent to a new home: {detail}
events.help: A resident is given a new home elsewhere: by the Dungeon Master's director (npc_relocate), or moved to a House's estate site; it walks there before the home changes.

events.title: Bandits rob a wagon
events.sentence: Bandits of {actor} rob the wagon to {target} in {cell}
events.help: Bandits camped on a road waylay a passing wagon and take its cargo.

actor.label: the bandit camp (its id, e.g. camp_<cell>)

target.label: the market the wagon was going to

events.title: Bandits make camp on a road
events.sentence: Bandits gather in {cell} on the road to {target}
events.help: Once a game week a new bandit camp may form in wild country along a road (never near a watch post).

actor.label: the new camp (its id, e.g. camp_<cell>)

target.label: the market at the road's far end

events.title: A bandit camp is broken
events.help: A bandit camp is broken: by whoever beat its last bandits, or by a town's watch on patrol.

actor.label: who cleared it (a character; the town's id when the watch did it)

target.label: the bandit camp (its id, e.g. camp_<cell>)

events.notes: tile only when a character cleared it and stands in that cell.

events.title: Bandits starve and scatter
events.sentence: The bandits of {actor} scatter, starved out
events.help: A bandit camp grown too hungry and weak breaks up on its own.

actor.label: the bandit camp (its id, e.g. camp_<cell>)

events.title: The watch goes after bandits
events.sentence: The watch of {actor} goes out after the bandits of {target}
events.help: A town with a bounty out on a camp sends its watch after the bandits (each game day, by chance).

actor.label: the town whose watch went out

target.label: the bandit camp (its id, e.g. camp_<cell>)

detail.label: 'the watch went out after the bandits'

events.title: A wagon arrives at a market
events.help: A wagon between markets reaches the far market and unloads.

events.title: A festival begins
events.help: A town's festival day reaches noon and the festival starts at the square.

events.title: A town project is finished
events.help: A town project has all its materials and work and stands built.
events.notes: actor carries the 'town:' prefix. The project's x,y are passed in the event's time slots and overwritten, so no tile is logged.

events.title: Someone gives to a town project
events.help: A wolf gives coins or hands in materials to a town project (or its upkeep).

item.label: the base item handed in, or 'coin'

events.notes: item is 'coin' for money.

events.title: Someone enters a festival contest
events.help: A wolf pays to enter a festival contest at the square, a board or an inn.

events.title: A carter loses the purse
events.sentence: {actor} is robbed by the bandits of {target}
events.help: A wagon is raided and its carter, not hurt, is robbed of the purse.

target.label: the bandit camp (its id, e.g. camp_<cell>)

detail.label: 'robbed of the purse in the raid'

events.notes: Logged with a raid, as the other half of 'carter hurt'.

events.title: A storyline objective is met
events.help: Something a character did met an objective of a storyline they are in (a personal storyline or a tale).

target.label: the storyline's id (a story run, a tale or a personal storyline)

detail.label: the objective's line, with ' (by hand)' when marked done by hand

events.title: A storyline step is done
events.help: Every objective of a storyline's step is met and the storyline moves to its next step.

target.label: the storyline's id (a story run, a tale or a personal storyline)

events.title: A tale ends
events.help: A storyteller's tale (a player-run storyline) is ended by its teller, or closed.

target.label: the storyline's id (a story run, a tale or a personal storyline)

events.title: A story enters a phase
events.help: A world story run (a campaign) is put into a phase by the story runner; recorded by the game.
events.notes: Triggers cannot listen for it (the runner refuses it as a trigger event); exits and the runner use it.

events.title: Someone does archive work
events.sentence: {actor} does {item} work at the archive in {cell}
events.help: A wolf does a task in a town's archive (copying, sorting records...) and is paid by the town.

detail.label: the town whose archive it is

events.title: Someone takes on a contract
events.help: A wolf takes on a posted contract (at a board, by letter), or a resident or town guard is given one (a guard taking an escort).

target.label: who posted it (a character or an account such as stores:<town>)

events.title: A contract is posted
events.help: Someone posts a contract with its reward held in trust: a town's escort for a wagon, a bounty on a camp, a courier's letter, a project's work.

actor.label: who posted it (a character or a town's store/treasury account)

target.label: what it is for: a bounty's camp, a courier's recipient, an escort's or supply's town

cell.label: where the poster is, when it is a character

events.notes: cell and tile only when the poster is a character in the world.

events.title: A deed is told of
events.help: A wolf's notable act becomes a deed in the town's talk (a camp broken, a project built, a promise kept, a trouble solved, a milestone credited...).

actor.label: the first of those who did it

target.label: who it was done for (a character, or 'town:<town id>')

item.label: the deed's kind (broke_camp, tended, kept_promise, carried_letter, built_project, award...)

detail.label: the deed in words, then its id in brackets

quantity.label: its weight: 0 small, 1 notable, 2 great, 3 legendary

events.notes: Only wolves are doers. target may be empty.

events.title: A festival contest is won
events.help: A festival contest ends with a winner and the pot is shared out.

actor.label: the winner (the first of a winning team)

coins.label: the winner's share of the pot

events.title: A fine is paid to the watch
events.help: Someone with a warrant pays what is owed and the fine to a guard who stopped them.

events.title: Someone forages
events.help: A wolf gathers from wild ground (alone, or the whole find of a joint foraging).

events.title: Someone is groomed
events.help: A wolf grooms another character, or itself.

events.title: A hunt begins
events.help: A wolf starts a hunt: animals are lined up in a hunting battle.

events.title: A part played in a hunt
events.help: When a hunt ends, one event for each part each wolf played; also when a wolf is given another's share to carry.

target.label: the role: tracker, driver, ambusher, carrier...

events.title: Someone gives their name
events.help: A character says one of its registered names to another, who learns it (hidden names on).

events.title: Someone rents lodging
events.help: A wolf rents a bed, a room upstairs at an inn, a lodger's place or a home's place.

item.label: the kind: bed, night, lodger, place

events.title: A lodging ends
events.help: A lodging runs out, is given up, can't be paid for, or ends because the place is held for a story.

item.label: the kind: bed, night, lodger, place

events.notes: tile only when the renter is in that place.

events.title: Something is lent
events.help: A wolf accepts a loan another offered: the goods move to the borrower until due.
events.notes: item may be a marked id (base~marks).

events.title: A letter is sent
events.help: A wolf hands a letter to the courier (paying the fee, perhaps with coins or goods enclosed).

target.label: the recipient (empty when it goes by a courier contract)

events.notes: An enclosure is not in the event; see 'letter returned'.

events.title: A letter is delivered
events.help: A letter reaches its reader, in their post town or at one of its inns.

cell.label: where the reader is (empty when it waits at an inn)

events.notes: cell and tile only when the reader is in the world.

events.title: A loan is given back
events.help: A borrower gives a loan back, or it falls due and the courier takes back what they still have (the whole loan).
events.notes: cell and tile only when the borrower is in the world (a loan falling due may come back while they are away). item may be a marked id.

events.title: A resident answers a notice
events.help: A resident answers a wolf's notice when it is posted: a seller or buyer for an item, a master for an apprenticeship.

item.label: what the notice is about: 'item:<item id>', 'apprenticeship:<trade>', 'room', 'partner'

events.title: A notice is posted
events.help: A wolf pins a notice on a board (seeking, offering, an event, lost, other) and pays the fee.

item.label: what it is about: 'item:<item id>', 'apprenticeship:<trade>', 'room', 'partner', or empty

events.title: A pact is sealed
events.help: Both parties to a pact (a written agreement sent by letter) have sealed it; recorded when the last of them seals.

events.title: Someone pays off bandits
events.help: A wolf stopped by bandits on the road pays what they demand (half the purse, if already fighting).

target.label: the bandit camp (its id, e.g. camp_<cell>)

events.title: Someone performs
events.help: A wolf begins to sing, tell a tale or play an instrument it carries, in a tavern or anywhere.

events.title: A crime is reported to the watch
events.help: A witness to a crime tells a guard of it.
events.notes: tile only when the witness is in the crime's cell.

events.title: A meal is shared
events.help: A wolf eats beside another who is eating too (within two tiles); once a game day for a pair.

events.title: A ship comes in
events.help: A ship on the timetable comes in to its port with its cargo.

events.title: A ship is lost at sea
events.sentence: {item} is lost at sea on the way to {target}
events.help: A ship due at a port is lost with all its cargo (by chance or by the Dungeon Master).

quantity.label: kinds of goods it was bringing

events.title: A ship sails
events.help: A docked ship leaves its port, taking goods with it.

quantity.label: pieces of goods it took on

events.title: A storm keeps a ship out
events.sentence: {item} is stormbound and will not come to {target}
events.help: A storm keeps a ship out of its port (by chance or by the Dungeon Master); what it brings grows dearer.

quantity.label: kinds of goods it was bringing

events.title: A market stall is rented
events.help: A wolf rents a stall at a market for the day.

events.title: Something is bought at a stall
events.help: Someone buys goods from a wolf's market stall.
events.notes: item may be a marked id.

events.title: A story is finished as a book
events.help: A chronicle story is finished and bound as a book; one event for each wolf in it.

events.title: A table game is won
events.help: A tavern table game ends with a winner, who takes the pot less the house's penny.

events.title: Someone is helped up
events.help: A character tends a downed one beside it and stands them up.

events.title: Two worked together
events.help: When a joint work (foraging, farm work, bench work) ends, one event for each pair who worked enough beats side by side.

events.title: A wolf is reported to the Wardens

events.title: A wolf hears of a trouble
events.help: A resident tells a wolf of a trouble of theirs in conversation.

events.help: A wolf solves a resident's trouble.

events.title: A wolf vouches to the Wardens

events.title: A cart stocks the Marketday stalls
events.sentence: The cart {actor} from {item} stocks the stalls at {target}
events.help: A farm's cart arrives on Marketday and fills the market's stalls.

events.title: A carter is hurt in a raid
events.sentence: {actor} is hurt by the bandits of {target}
events.help: A wagon is raided and its carter is bruised (half the time; else 'carter robbed').

target.label: the bandit camp (its id, e.g. camp_<cell>)

events.title: A new wolf is made
events.help: A player makes a new character.
events.notes: The wolf is not in the world yet, so no cell or tile.

events.title: A fallen spawned resident is cleared
events.help: A spawn rule clears away one of its spawned residents who has fallen, before spawning another.
events.notes: Nothing to do with bandits, despite doc 85's grouping: it comes from DM spawn rules (RatwGame.cpp:2344).

events.title: A contract is given back
events.help: A wolf gives up a contract it had taken; it is open again.

events.title: The town crier cries
events.help: A town's crier (its official, an innkeeper or the priest) cries a news line, or the season's deeds and nicknames, at the square.

detail.label: the line cried (news), or the festival's name (deeds)

quantity.label: lines of news (1), or deeds called

events.notes: tile only when the crier already stands in the square's cell.

events.title: A deed is revoked
events.help: The Dungeon Master strikes a deed from the record; the town forgets it.
events.notes: Only detail is filled.

events.title: Someone goes down in a fight
events.help: A fighter (or an animal in a hunt) is knocked down in a battle.
events.notes: tile = where the fallen one lies in the fight, not the actor's. A bandit going down also records 'bandit falls'.

events.title: The Dungeon Master adds a market event
events.sentence: The market event {actor} is added at {target}: {detail}
events.help: The Dungeon Master adds an event to a market's calendar (a fair, a shortage, a glut...).
events.notes: No cell. Its notice, if due already, follows as 'event posted'.

events.title: A market event begins
events.help: A market event's day arrives and it takes effect on prices and stock.

detail.label: its notice, or its words when it has none

quantity.label: 1 if it was not announced before, else 0

events.title: A market event's notice changes
events.sentence: The notice of market event {actor} at {target} changes
events.help: A market event tied to a ship gets its after-notice once that ship has sailed (or is gone).

events.title: A market event is announced
events.sentence: The market event {actor} is announced at {target}
events.help: A coming market event's notice goes up on the board, some days before it begins.

events.title: A market event is rolled
events.sentence: A market event {actor} is rolled for {target}
events.help: The staged economy rolls a new event onto a market's calendar.

events.title: A fight starts
events.help: A fight begins: a character attacks another, or bandits rush or attack a wolf on the road.

actor.label: the attacker (or the bandit camp's id when bandits start it)

detail.label: the battle's id, or 'bandits rush' / 'bandits attack'

events.notes: tile only when a character attacks (none for bandits).

events.title: A season's harvest is called
events.sentence: The harvest of {actor} is called for {target}
events.help: The Dungeon Master calls a poor, fair or good season for a harvest area; posted on the boards of its markets (one event per market).

target.label: a market it is posted at

detail.label: the notice, e.g. 'A good season for wheat and oats.'

events.title: A place is held for a story
events.help: The Dungeon Master or a story holds a place: no new lodgings, running ones given a week's notice.

events.title: A letter's enclosure comes back
events.help: A letter holding coins or goods goes back to its writer with them: unread for 56 game days, its reader gone, or burnt unopened.
events.notes: Recorded only when there was an enclosure to return. cell and tile when the writer is in the world.

events.title: A loan isn't given back
events.help: A loan falls due and the borrower no longer has all of it: the rest is owed to the lender.
events.notes: cell and tile only when the borrower is in the world.

events.title: A resident points out a companion
events.help: A resident talking to a newcomer wolf suggests another wolf they might meet (doc 52).

events.title: A story milestone is credited
events.help: The Dungeon Master's host credits a world story's milestone to the wolves who took part (deeds follow for the main ones).

events.title: A resident mourns
events.help: Someone dies and each resident close to them (family, or a good friend) begins to mourn.

events.title: A wolf is given a nickname
events.help: After a notable deed (or a third small one), a resident who likes the wolf coins a nickname for it.
events.notes: tile only when the wolf is in the deed's cell.

events.title: A nickname is dropped
events.help: A wolf drops one of its nicknames; it is never coined again from that deed.

events.title: A notice is taken down
events.sentence: The notice {detail} of {actor} is taken down
events.help: The Dungeon Master takes a notice off a board.
events.notes: cell and tile only when the author is in the world.

events.title: A Times nudge lapses
events.sentence: The nudge to trade at {actor} is over
events.help: A Dungeon Master's nudge to a market's Times runs out or is cleared.

events.title: A resident dies of age
events.help: A resident dies by the daily chance of its age (after 'death').

detail.label: 'died of old age' (60 or older) or 'died'

events.title: A market's prices are reset
events.help: The Dungeon Master resets the prices of one market or all (one event per market).

detail.label: the words given, default 'fresh stock everywhere'

events.title: A town project is cancelled
events.help: A town project is called off (by the Dungeon Master) and its gifts refunded.

detail.label: why, e.g. 'cancelled by the Dungeon Master'

events.title: A town project is posted
events.help: A town project is put up for gifts and work: by the town's own needs, the Dungeon Master or a developer.
events.notes: The project's x,y are passed in the event's time slots and overwritten, so no tile is logged. A town's own proposal also records 'project proposed'.

events.title: A town proposes a project
events.help: A town decides it needs something (cover, mending...) and posts a project of its own.

cell.label: where it will stand (may be empty)

events.notes: Follows a 'project posted' with actor 'town'.

events.title: A town project is removed
events.help: A town project (built or not) is removed and its gifts refunded.

events.title: A promise is made
events.help: In conversation (not the dialogue window) the NPC Mind reports a promise: by the resident to the wolf, or by the wolf to the resident.
events.notes: Kept if the promiser trades with, pays, gives to or helps the other within 3 days ('promise kept', not listed); else 'promise broken'.

events.title: A promise is broken
events.help: A promise falls due without being kept.

events.title: Someone is let out of the gaol
events.help: Someone held by the watch has served their time.

events.title: A resident writes to a wolf
events.help: A resident writes to a wolf (thanks for help, a wedding or funeral invitation, work offered...), perhaps with coins.

events.title: Bandits beat and rob a wolf
events.sentence: The bandits of {actor} beat and rob {target}
events.help: Bandits beat a wolf to the ground in a road fight and take half its purse.

actor.label: the bandit camp (its id, e.g. camp_<cell>)

events.title: A sermon is preached
events.help: A priest reaches the pulpit and begins the week's sermon.

events.title: A ship is put on the timetable
events.help: The wharf's timetable gains a ship due at a port.

quantity.label: kinds of goods it will bring

events.notes: detail is '<Name>, due <weekday>.'.

events.title: A port's ship notice comes down
events.help: A port's ships notice comes down: no ships due any more, or its port is gone.

cell.label: the port (empty when it is gone)

events.notes: Its twin 'ships posted' (the notice put up) is not listed.

events.title: A resident is spawned
events.help: A Dungeon Master's spawn rule puts a new resident into its area.

events.title: A market stall closes
events.help: A rented stall closes at the day's end (or is given up); its goods go back to the keeper.
events.notes: tile only when the keeper is still in that place.

events.title: Stolen goods are smelt
events.help: A resident's nose catches its own maker's scent on goods a thief carries: it now knows of the theft.

events.title: The watch stops someone
events.help: A guard confronts someone with a warrant: pay, or come along.

events.title: A story's prize is given
events.help: A storyteller gives a prize from their purse (or an Officer from the Chapter's) for their tale.

events.title: A storyline begins
events.help: A character starts a storyline (a personal quest, from a template or a source).

target.label: the storyline's id (a story run, a tale or a personal storyline)

events.title: A storyline is finished
events.help: Every step of a storyline is done.

target.label: the storyline's id (a story run, a tale or a personal storyline)

events.title: A table game begins
events.help: A wolf starts a tavern table game with the players seated.

item.label: the game: knucklebones, wolves or liars

events.title: A tale begins
events.help: A storyteller starts (or resumes) their tale.

target.label: the storyline's id (a story run, a tale or a personal storyline)

events.title: A wolf joins a tale
events.help: An invited wolf accepts a part in a tale.

target.label: the storyline's id (a story run, a tale or a personal storyline)

events.title: A newcomer tie ends
events.help: A newcomer's tie with a mentor is ended by the host or the Dungeon Master.
events.notes: A player ending their own tie from the client is not logged.

events.title: The Times' cause is told
events.help: The economy's slider moves and its cause is told once in every market (a notice and a crier's line).

events.title: Trade at a market is nudged
events.help: The Dungeon Master nudges a market's Times up or down for some days; posted once.

detail.label: the notice ('Trade is brisk in ...' or the cause)

events.title: A vouch goes bad
events.help: A newcomer someone vouched for wrongs the resident they were vouched to.

events.title: A wagon departure is cancelled
events.help: A committed wagon (or cart) departure can't go: its market is gone, the road is closed, or no carter for too long.

cell.label: the setting-out market's place (empty when that market is gone)

item.label: where it was to set out from (a market, or a farm's id for a cart)

events.title: A wagon departure is put off
events.sentence: The wagon {actor} to {target} is put off a day
events.help: A committed wagon has no carter or no room on the roads, and goes a day later.

item.label: the market it sets out from

events.title: A wagon departure is posted
events.sentence: A wagon from {item} to {target} is posted
events.help: The staged economy commits a wagon between two markets and posts its notices.

item.label: the market it sets out from

quantity.label: kinds of goods it will carry

events.title: An innkeeper welcomes a newcomer
events.help: An innkeeper welcomes a newcomer wolf and points out others who could help them.

events.title: A wolf comes back after a while
events.help: A wolf comes back into the world after days away and is told what happened meanwhile.

events.title: Time passes in the phase
events.sentence: The phase has been open a while
events.help: The story runner's clock: fires once the phase has been open the trigger's afterDays game days.
events.notes: No fields. The delay is the trigger's afterDays (from 1/1440, a minute, to 36,500 days), counted from when the phase opened.

events.title: The Dungeon Master gives a direction
events.help: The Dungeon Master sends a named direction from the Campaigns tab; it can only move a phase through an exit (never a trigger).

actor.label: the wolf it is sent as, if any

events.notes: Exits only. Made by the story runner, never in game.events. Tried as a story signal of the same name first.

events.title: A story signal arrives
events.help: A named signal sent by another trigger (emit), by a timer (schedule) or by the Dungeon Master.

actor.label: the wolf it concerns, if any

events.notes: Not in game.events. An emitted signal keeps the source event's actor, target, cell, item, detail, quantity, coins and tile; a timer's carries only the timer's owner as actor. Each name is delivered at most once per world event, after that event's triggers. The catalogue has a 'signal' type for the name.

events.title: The missions are done
events.sentence: The phase's chosen missions are complete
events.help: An exit that waits until every mission it names has reached its completion threshold, for a wolf in the phase's cohort.
events.notes: Exits only (not a trigger). Its parameter is the list 'missions' (ids of this phase's missions), not an event field.

events.title: The phase is ready
events.sentence: The phase's Readiness is met (or an admin presses Advance)
events.help: The way on when the phase is ready: every part of its Readiness met (enough of the active wolves took part, enough days in the phase or the chapter, values, missions, a quest). With auto it is taken by itself (at once, or at the moment `then` names); otherwise the Campaigns console says it is ready and an admin presses Advance.
events.notes: Exits only, and only in a phase with "ready" (exactly one). Taken by the story runner, never by a world event. Its only fields are on and to.

events.title: A wolf takes on a quest
events.help: A wolf accepted a story's quest: in the giver's dialogue window, or from the journal for a quest offered to them. The story checks who may take it (its join rules) and starts their copy.

item.label: the resident it was taken from (empty: from the journal)

events.title: A wolf declines a quest
events.help: A wolf said not now to a story's quest offered to them; it can be asked about again.

item.label: the resident it was taken from (empty: from the journal)

events.title: A wolf hands in a quest
events.help: A wolf whose quest was ready came back to its giver and handed it in (the dialogue window's hand-in choice): the quest is done and its rewards are given.

events.title: A wolf abandons a quest
events.help: A wolf put a story's quest aside from the journal.

events.title: A wolf picks a story's choice in a dialogue window
events.help: A wolf picked a story choice laid over a resident's dialogue window (npc.offer): the wolf's words said, the resident's reply given.

events.title: A wolf joins a party
events.help: A wolf joined a party (accepted an invitation). Stories keep each wolf's party from these: party quests and party variables.

events.title: A wolf leaves a party
events.help: A wolf left a party, or the party was disbanded (one event for each of its wolves).

events.title: A story's quest starts
events.help: The story's own fact (never in the world's log): a copy of a quest began for a wolf, their party or the story.
events.notes: Sent by the story itself as it runs, after the fact that caused it; the game never records it.

events.title: A story's quest is done
events.help: The story's own fact: a copy of a quest was completed (handed in, or its last required objective done); its rewards follow.
events.notes: Sent by the story itself as it runs, after the fact that caused it; the game never records it.

events.title: A story's quest fails
events.help: The story's own fact: a copy of a quest failed (a fail rule, its deadline, an objective failed, or by hand).
events.notes: Sent by the story itself as it runs, after the fact that caused it; the game never records it.

events.title: A quest's objective is done
events.help: The story's own fact: an objective of a quest copy was done.
events.notes: Sent by the story itself as it runs, after the fact that caused it; the game never records it.

events.title: A wolf opens a door
events.help: A wolf opened a door (or walked through a closed one, which opens it). Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A wolf closes a door
events.help: A wolf closed a door. Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A wolf tries a locked door
events.help: A wolf tried to open a locked door. Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A wolf goes indoors
events.help: A wolf went from out of doors (or another room) into an interior: a building, a room, a cellar. Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A wolf comes out of a building
events.help: A wolf left an interior. Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A region is no longer empty
events.sentence: {actor} is the first of the story's wolves in {target}
events.help: The count of the story's wolves standing in one of its regions went from none to one (quantity: the count). Signing in inside it counts. Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A region is empty again
events.sentence: {actor} was the last of the story's wolves to leave {target}
events.help: The last of the story's wolves standing in one of its regions left it (or signed out inside it). Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: The weather changes
events.help: The weather in a place the story watches changed (a place it names, or where one of the world's wolves stands). Checked every few seconds. Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

detail.label: the new weather (clear, overcast, rain, storm, fog, snow, sandstorm)

events.title: An hour of the day begins
events.help: The world's clock reached a new hour (quantity: the hour, 0 to 23; detail: the same as text, "14"). Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A new day begins
events.help: Midnight: a new day of the world's calendar (detail: the weekday, Marketday, Restday...; item: the season; quantity: the day of the season). Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: Dawn
events.help: The light comes up (5 o'clock). Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: Night falls
events.help: Full dark (19 o'clock). Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A season begins
events.help: The first day of a season (detail: spring, summer, autumn or winter). Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A wolf picks up an item
events.help: A wolf picked up something lying on the ground (what was knocked loose in a fight). Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A wolf drops an item
events.help: A wolf's held item fell to the ground (knocked loose in a fight). Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A wolf buys or sells
events.help: A wolf bought from or sold to a trader (a shop, a stall's keeper): detail is bought or sold, coins what changed hands. Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A wolf opens a resident's window
events.help: A wolf opened a resident's dialogue window (doc 83): detail is what they opened it on (resident, trade, missions, introduce...). Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A dialogue reaches a node
events.help: A resident's dialogue window moved to a node of its tree (detail: the node's id, item: the tree's id); a story's own nodes are @story:<run>:<kind>:<id>. Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A wolf leaves a resident's window
events.help: A resident's dialogue window closed (detail: why: end, bye, walked away, replaced...). Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A crime is seen
events.help: Someone noticed a crime as it happened (a theft, an attempted theft, a blow): the witness (a wolf or a resident), the offender, the victim, the kind. Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

target.label: the offender (empty when the witness could not tell who)

events.title: A wolf goes down
events.help: One of the world's wolves was knocked down (in a fight, or beaten by bandits). Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A wolf is back on their feet
events.help: A downed wolf got up, or was tended back to their feet (target: who tended them, if anyone). Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A party is formed
events.help: A new party came together (an invitation accepted): its leader. Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A party breaks up
events.help: A party ended (disbanded, or down to one). Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A wolf comes near a resident
events.help: A wolf comes within three tiles of a resident the trigger names (the moving location: wherever the resident is now), in the same place; again only after they have been more than five tiles apart. Name the resident. Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).
events.notes: Looked at once a second while a story listens: the residents named in the filters of its triggers and exits.

events.title: A purse crosses an amount
events.help: A town's treasury, its works, watch or church, a till or a Chapter's purse (as a reward names one: town:<town>, town:<town>:works, till:<id>, chapter:<id>) goes up or down past an amount the trigger names in its detail (quantity: what it holds now). Name the purse and the amount. Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).
events.notes: Looked at every two seconds while a story listens; the first look makes no event.

events.title: A wolf's standing crosses a number
events.help: A wolf in the world: their standing with a faction (their Chapter's, as the faction counts it) goes up or down past a number the trigger names in its detail (quantity: the standing now). Name the faction and the number. Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).
events.notes: Looked at every two seconds for the wolves in the world while a story listens; a wolf first looked at makes no event.

events.title: A faction's stance changes
events.help: One faction's stance toward another changed (a DM's change, a story's, or the world's own): the new stance (quantity: the disposition). Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A resident takes a mantle
events.help: A resident now wears a mantle (doc 84: a dialogue of their own), by a DM's hand, a story's, or a mantle loaded again. Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A resident lays a mantle down
events.help: A resident no longer wears the mantle they wore. Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A wolf's skill grows a step
events.help: A wolf's skill passes a whole step by practice (quantity: the new whole value), as their growth lines say. Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: A wolf's injury heals
events.help: An injury of a wolf healed with rest: the injury in words. Written only while a live story listens for it (the story's watch list).

events.title: Another story starts
events.help: Another story of this world was published, or started by a chapter before it (story.start): its id, not its run, so one chapter can wait for another.

detail.label: the campaign it is a chapter of

events.notes: Sent by the story runner to every other live story of the world that listens for it; never in the world's log.

events.title: Another story ends
events.help: Another story of this world ended: complete, success, failure, abandoned or stopped (by an admin).

detail.label: how it ended: complete, success, failure, abandoned, stopped

events.notes: Sent by the story runner to every other live story of the world that listens for it; never in the world's log.

conditions.title: All of these
conditions.help: True when every condition under it is true (1 to 8).

conditions.title: Any of these
conditions.help: True when one condition under it is true.

conditions.title: Not
conditions.help: True when the condition under it is false.

conditions.title: The event's field
conditions.help: Compares one field of the event that just happened. Text takes = and !=; quantity and coins take a number.

conditions.title: A counter
conditions.help: Compares one of the story's counters with a number. A player counter is the acting wolf's.

conditions.title: Inside a region
conditions.help: The event's tile is inside the rectangle. An event with no tile is unknown, and unknown never fires, not even under "not".

conditions.title: A mission is ready
conditions.help: That mission of the current phase has reached its completion threshold. Phase triggers only.

conditions.title: Compare two values
conditions.help: Compares two values of one kind: variables, the event's fields, numbers, texts, a list's count, a timer's days, a little arithmetic. Numbers take any comparison; switches and texts take = and !=. A value of a wolf not in the story makes it false.

conditions.title: A switch is on or off
conditions.help: A declared switch is on, or off.

conditions.title: A value is in a list
conditions.help: A value (the acting wolf, the event's item, a text) is one of a list variable's.

conditions.title: The story is in a phase
conditions.sentence: the story is in the phase {phase}
conditions.help: For campaign triggers: true in that phase only.

conditions.title: The phase's visit
conditions.sentence: this is visit {op} {value} of the phase
conditions.help: The run's visit number (1 the first time the story is in a phase, then one more each time it moves).

conditions.title: A timer is running
conditions.sentence: the timer {signal} ({owner}) is running, with {op} {days} days left
conditions.help: A named timer (Start a timer) is running; with a comparison, it has that many days left. A timer that has gone off is not running.

conditions.title: A trigger has fired
conditions.sentence: the trigger {trigger} has fired {op} {value} times this {in}
conditions.help: How often a trigger of this story fired, this phase visit or this run (Run counts; a trigger firing by hand counts).

conditions.title: A chance
conditions.help: True that many times in 100, rolled when it is asked: seeded by the run, so a replay gives the same answer; a rehearsal case may pin its rolls.

conditions.title: Days since
conditions.help: Game days since the phase opened or the run began, or days (on its own clock) since a timer variable started.

conditions.title: A wolf is in the world
conditions.help: The wolf is signed in now (as of the event). A wolf away is not here: this is never unknown while the world's facts are known.

conditions.title: A wolf stands in a region
conditions.help: Where the wolf stands now (as of the event), inside the story's region. Unknown for a wolf away.

conditions.title: A wolf is in a place
conditions.help: The wolf is in that cell or interior now. Unknown for a wolf away.

conditions.title: A wolf is in a town
conditions.help: The wolf is somewhere in that town's cells (indoors too). Unknown for a wolf away.

conditions.title: A wolf is indoors
conditions.help: The wolf is under a roof (an interior), or out of doors. Unknown for a wolf away.

conditions.title: How many stand in a region
conditions.sentence: {op} {value} of the story's wolves stand in {region}
conditions.help: Counts the wolves of the story standing in the region now (StarCraft's Bring). Wolves away are not counted.

conditions.title: A wolf carries an item
conditions.help: How many of an item the wolf has in their pack (marked or crafted ones count as their base item). Unknown for a wolf away.

conditions.title: A wolf's coins
conditions.help: The coins in the wolf's own purse. Unknown for a wolf away.

conditions.title: Standing with a faction
conditions.help: The standing of the wolf's Chapter with a faction or House (-100 to 100; only Chapters have standing). Unknown for a wolf with no Chapter, or away.

conditions.title: Reputation in a town
conditions.help: What the town's residents who know the wolf think of them: those who like them less those who dislike them. 0 where nobody knows them. Unknown for a wolf away.

conditions.title: A wolf is downed, hurt, wanted or held
conditions.help: Downed (knocked down, not yet up), hurt (carrying wounds or an injury), wanted (a warrant of the watch), held (in a town's gaol). Unknown for a wolf away.

conditions.title: A wolf's party
conditions.help: How many wolves are in the wolf's party, the wolf included (1: alone). Unknown for a wolf away.

conditions.title: In a party with another wolf
conditions.help: Both wolves are in the world and in one party.

conditions.title: A resident is alive, dead or indoors
conditions.help: A named resident is alive, dead, or indoors now (as of the event).

conditions.title: A resident is in a place
conditions.help: A named resident is in that cell or interior now.

conditions.title: A resident stands in a region
conditions.help: A named resident stands inside the story's region now.

conditions.title: A resident's job, mood or mantle
conditions.help: A named resident's job (the kind of work, as residents' talk names it: guard, merchant, smith, farmer...), their mood now (even, bright, low or sore), the mantle they wear (doc 84), or the town they live in.

conditions.title: The hour
conditions.help: The world's hour (0 to 23), from one hour to another, both included; from 22 to 4 runs through midnight.

conditions.title: The day, the season, the time of day
conditions.help: The weekday (Marketday, Restday...), the season, or the time of day (dawn, day, dusk, night).

conditions.title: The weather
conditions.help: The weather in a place now: where the acting wolf is, or a named place. Indoors it is the weather outside.

conditions.title: How one faction stands with another
conditions.help: One faction's stance toward another, in the order war, hostile, tense, neutral, friendly, allied: ">=" is at least, "<=" at most.

conditions.title: A quest's state
conditions.help: Where a quest stands for the acting wolf (or the looped one; their party's copy for a party quest), or the story's one copy: none (never taken), offered, active, ready (to hand in), done, failed, abandoned, expired.

conditions.title: An objective's state
conditions.help: An objective of a quest, in the acting wolf's (or the looped one's, or the story's) copy: done, failed, to do (neither yet), or hidden (not yet shown). Without a copy it is to do, or hidden.

conditions.title: Enough wolves took part
conditions.sentence: at least {percent}% of the {of} wolves (at least {floor}; {cap}) {source} {list}{where}
conditions.help: Counts the story's wolves who are active (seen in the last activeDays game days; or all of them, or those online now) and, of those, the ones in a list of wolves or the ones for whom a test is true. True when they are at least the share asked and at least the floor (the floor never asks for more wolves than are active; a cap, if given, is always enough, so a crowd of 3,000 does not need 1,000). With no active wolves it is false; with the online wolves not known it is unknown. A wolf who did it and then went quiet leaves both counts, so the share stays honest.

actions.title: Set a counter
actions.help: Sets a counter, clamped to plus or minus 1,000,000,000.

actions.title: Add to a counter
actions.help: Adds to a counter (a negative number takes away).

actions.title: Send a signal
actions.help: A named signal, delivered after this event's triggers; it keeps the event's actor, item, target, place, amounts and detail.

actions.title: Start a timer
actions.sentence: Start the timer {signal} to go off in {days} days on the {clock} clock, {owner}, for {scope}{repeat}
actions.help: A named timer that sends the signal when due. The same name for the same owner replaces the deadline. The shortest delay is a minute (1/1440 of a day).

actions.title: Cancel a timer
actions.help: Stops that timer.

actions.title: Set a variable
actions.help: Sets a declared variable to a value of its kind (a number is kept within plus or minus 1,000,000,000).

actions.title: Add to a number
actions.help: Adds to a number variable (a negative number takes away).

actions.title: Take from a number
actions.help: Subtracts from a number variable.

actions.title: Multiply a number
actions.help: Multiplies a number variable.

actions.title: Keep a number between two
actions.help: Raises a number to the lower bound, or lowers it to the upper one.

actions.title: Turn a switch on
actions.help: A switch, on.

actions.title: Turn a switch off
actions.help: A switch, off.

actions.title: Flip a switch
actions.help: A switch, the other way.

actions.title: Remember who or what
actions.help: Keeps an id from the event (the acting wolf, the target, the item, the place, the detail) or the loop's value in a variable: the wolf who found the pup.

actions.title: Add to a list
actions.help: Adds a value to a list variable, once (a list holds up to 500).

actions.title: Take out of a list
actions.help: Removes a value from a list variable.

actions.title: Empty a list
actions.help: Removes every value.

actions.title: Pick one from a list
actions.sentence: Pick one of {list} at random as {of} {var}
actions.help: Puts one value of a list, chosen at random (seeded), into a variable of its kind. An empty list leaves it as it was.

actions.title: Start a timer variable
actions.help: Sets a timer variable to now (its clock); Days since and "since" count from it.

actions.title: Clear a timer variable
actions.help: Unsets a timer variable: Days since it is false until it starts again.

actions.title: Move a timer
actions.help: Moves a running timer's deadline later, or earlier with a negative number.

actions.title: If, else if, else
actions.help: Runs the actions under the first condition that holds (If, then each Else if), or those under Else. Nests three deep with For each and Random.

actions.title: Wait
actions.help: The rest of the actions run later, for the same wolf and with the same event. It ends with the phase visit, unless it is a campaign trigger's; it never holds up another trigger. At least a minute of the world's clock, or 5 seconds of the real one (coarse: tight timing belongs in a scene). Not inside For each.

actions.title: For each
actions.help: Runs the actions once for each wolf of the story, of the acting wolf's party, or each value of a list (500 at most). The value is $each: the looped wolf, in effects and in variables of each wolf. Not inside another For each.

actions.title: Random
actions.help: Runs one of 2 to 8 lists of actions, each as likely as its weight. Seeded: a replay or a rehearsal gives the same pick.

actions.title: Run another trigger
actions.help: Runs another trigger's actions now, for the same wolf and event, checking whether it is on and its conditions, or not. A trigger may not run itself, or one that runs it back.

words.true: if it is on and its conditions hold

actions.title: Turn a trigger on
actions.help: Turns a trigger on (one that starts off, or one turned off). From the next event: the triggers of the event that turned it on have been chosen.

actions.title: Turn a trigger off
actions.help: Turns a trigger off until turned on again (it stays off on a later visit of its phase).

actions.title: Skip the rest
actions.help: Ends this trigger's actions here.

actions.title: A note for the DM
actions.help: A line in the campaign's timeline and the rehearsal's trace, and nowhere in the world: the debugging message.

actions.title: End the story
actions.help: Ends the run with an outcome and a line for the chronicle; for one wolf, gives them their own ending and the story goes on.

actions.title: Change the world
actions.help: Asks the game to change the world: one of the world effects below. Each is a DM order the game checks again when it applies it.

actions.title: Go to a phase
actions.help: Moves the story to a phase. Must be the last action.

effects.title: Play a scene
effects.help: Plays one of the scenes embedded in this story; a public scene may play for the world.

effects.title: Give a resident a dialogue line
effects.sentence: {npc} has the line {text} for the story's wolves
effects.help: Phase entry only: while the phase is open the resident has this line for the wolves of the story.

effects.title: A resident walks somewhere
effects.help: The resident goes there; "scene arrived" follows (or "scene blocked" after 180 seconds without progress).

effects.title: A resident speaks
effects.help: The resident says it aloud; "scene spoken" follows.

effects.title: A resident takes a posture
effects.help: The resident stands, sits or lies down; "scene posed" follows.

effects.title: Hurt the wolves in a region
effects.sentence: Hurt the story's wolves inside {region} by {points} points
effects.help: Acts on players' wolves: needs "may act on players' wolves" on a hosted world.

effects.title: Give an item to the wolves in a region
effects.sentence: Give each of the story's wolves inside {region} {quantity} {item}
effects.help: A full pack is skipped and the wolf told.

effects.title: Feed the wolves in a region
effects.sentence: The story's wolves inside {region} are {buff} for {hours} hours
effects.help: The timed "fed" benefit.

effects.title: A bandit camp in a region
effects.help: Bandits camp in the rectangle.

effects.title: Put a resident somewhere
effects.help: The resident is there at once (no walk).

effects.title: Protect a resident
effects.help: Marks the resident as one who cannot be killed.

effects.title: Remove a resident's protection
effects.help: Takes the mark off.

effects.title: Revive a resident
effects.help: Brings a dead resident back.

effects.title: Injure a wolf
effects.help: Acts on players' wolves: needs "may act on players' wolves" on a hosted world.

effects.title: Hold a ship in a storm
effects.help: A ship due in port is held by a storm.

effects.title: Set a harvest
effects.sentence: The harvest in {area} is {word} for {days} days ({words})
effects.help: Sets a harvest area's yield for a while; "clear" gives it back to the season.

effects.title: Set a household's prosperity
effects.help: A household's prosperity band for a while.

effects.title: Call a festival
effects.help: Schedules a festival.

effects.title: Give a personal quest
effects.sentence: Give {player} the personal quest {template} with {resident} at {place}
effects.help: Starts a personal quest from a DM template; refused at three personal quests.

effects.title: Change faction relations
effects.help: One faction's stance toward another. A builder or the owner must approve it on a hosted world.

effects.title: Send bandits after a wolf
effects.help: The wolf must be in the world.

effects.title: Give a wolf a lesson
effects.help: A lesson under the ordinary practice rules; the wolf must be in the world.

effects.title: Change market conditions
effects.sentence: Push the times in {market} by {points} for {days} days ({words})
effects.help: Pushes a market's times up or down for a while.

effects.title: Award a deed
effects.help: A deed on the wolf's fame; the wolf must be in the world.

effects.title: Post a town project
effects.help: Opens a town project.

effects.title: Offer a quest
effects.help: The wolf is offered the quest: they accept or decline it in its giver's window, or in the journal when it has no giver. Takes the wolf into the story.

effects.title: Start a quest
effects.help: Gives the quest without asking: the wolf's own copy, their party's, or the story's one copy. Takes the wolf into the story.

effects.title: Complete a quest
effects.help: Completes the copy the wolf holds, as if its last objective were done: its rewards are given.

effects.title: Fail a quest
effects.help: Fails the copy the wolf holds; the journal says so.

effects.title: Complete an objective
effects.help: Marks one objective of the copy the wolf holds done (a hidden one is shown).

effects.title: Fail an objective
effects.help: An optional objective failed is struck through; a required one failed fails the quest.

effects.title: Reveal a hidden objective
effects.help: A hidden objective appears in the journal.

effects.title: Add to an objective
effects.help: Counts towards an objective's goal as if its event had happened that many times (or that quantity).

effects.title: Take a wolf into the story
effects.help: The wolf joins the story's audience (an open audience's way in), up to its cap: they see it in their journal.

effects.title: Take a wolf out of the story
effects.help: The wolf leaves the story's audience; quests they hold are abandoned.

effects.title: Offer a choice in a resident's window
effects.sentence: {npc} offers the choice {id} to {player}: the wolf says {words}, {npc} replies {reply} (once: {once})
effects.help: While this phase visit is open, the resident's dialogue window shows a story choice to the wolf (or every wolf of the story): the wolf's words, the resident's reply in their own voice. Picking it makes a 'dialogue choice' event.

params.label: who sees it (empty: every wolf of the story)

effects.title: Pay a wolf from a purse
effects.help: Coins from a named purse (a town, its works, a business's till, a Chapter), never made from nothing: refused when the purse is short or over the wolf's day of grants.

effects.title: Give a wolf an item
effects.help: An item into one wolf's pack; a full pack is refused and the wolf told.

effects.title: Change a wolf's standing
effects.help: A few points of standing with a faction, for a reason the wolf is told. A builder or the owner must approve it on a hosted world.

effects.title: Tell the wolves
effects.help: A line to one wolf, a wolf's party, the story's wolves, the wolves standing in a region, or everyone in the world: a banner and a line in their log. A wolf of the story who is away is told when back; nobody away refuses it.

effects.title: Add a note to the journal
effects.help: A line under the story in the wolf's journal (or every wolf's of the story), kept with the story: the newest 12.

effects.title: Mark a place on the map
effects.sentence: Mark {cell,x,y} on the maps of {player} as {label} for {minutes} minutes
effects.help: A marker on the minimap and the World Map of the story's wolves (or one wolf's) for a while. Undone when the story ends.

effects.title: Show or hide a tracker
effects.help: A shown variable (its "shown as" label) among the story's trackers in the wolves' journal: shown again, or hidden for now.

effects.title: Take an item from a wolf
effects.help: Out of one wolf's pack (gone, not paid for). Refused when they carry fewer. Acts on players' wolves: needs "may act on players' wolves" on a hosted world.

effects.title: Mark a wolf wanted
effects.sentence: {player} is wanted by the watch of {town}, fined {fine}p: {reason}
effects.help: A warrant from a town's watch, as for a crime: its guards stop the wolf for the fine or the gaol. Acts on players' wolves: needs "may act on players' wolves" on a hosted world.

effects.title: Lift a warrant
effects.help: The town's watch no longer wants the wolf (what was owed is forgiven). Refused when there is no warrant.

effects.title: Bring a stranger
effects.sentence: {name} ({visitor}) comes to {cell,x,y} for {minutes} minutes, looking like {like} {description}
effects.help: A temporary resident appears at the tile for a while, then goes (the spawn). Their id is the story's own: Send away names it. Sent away when the story ends.

effects.title: Send a stranger away
effects.help: A temporary resident the story brought goes.

effects.title: Bind a mantle
effects.help: A mantle (doc 84: a part with its own lines in the dialogue window) bound to the resident. Released when the story ends.

effects.title: Release a mantle
effects.help: The resident's mantle is released.

effects.title: A resident dies
effects.help: The resident dies where they stand (Bring back undoes it). Never a protected resident.

effects.title: Hold a resident
effects.help: Off their schedule: they stay where they stand (or where a walk takes them) for the story, and no other story may direct them. Released by Release, or when the story ends.

effects.title: Release a resident
effects.help: A resident the story held goes back to their day.

effects.title: A resident follows a wolf
effects.help: The resident joins the wolf's party (or makes one with them) for the story's sake and follows. Refused when the party is full or the resident cannot leave. They go home when the story ends.

effects.title: A resident stops following
effects.help: A resident the story sent along goes home.

effects.title: Lock a door
effects.help: Both sides of the door are locked (it closes first). Unlocked again when the story ends.

effects.title: Unlock a door
effects.help: Both sides of a locked door are unlocked. Locked again when the story ends.

effects.title: Open a door
effects.help: The door stands open (an unlocked one). It stays as a wolf would leave it.

effects.title: Close a door
effects.help: The door is shut. It stays as a wolf would leave it.

effects.title: Leave an item on the ground
effects.help: Things to be found and picked up, by anyone. They lie there until taken (or the server restarts).

effects.title: Pin a notice to a board
effects.sentence: Pin to the board of {town} for {days} days: {text}
effects.help: A notice on the town's board, signed with the story's title. Taken down when the story ends.

effects.title: Set the weather
effects.sentence: The weather in {place} {town} is {weather} for {hours} hours
effects.help: The weather of a place out of doors, or of every street of a town, for some hours of the world's clock, then the season's again. Harvests and the cold follow it. A story never changes the day or the hour. On a hosted world it needs what the same act by hand on LIVE needs (a Dungeon Master). Undone when the story ends.

effects.title: Stage a market event
effects.help: One of the market's events (a wedding, a fire, a glut) staged for today or within the next week, under the rules the scheduler keeps.

words.lame_ox: the lame ox that held up the from cart

effects.title: Call off a market event
effects.help: The next such event at the market still to come or on is called off.

words.lame_ox: the lame ox that held up the from cart

effects.title: Ease prices back
effects.sentence: Prices at {market} ease back to their usual: {words}
effects.help: A market's prices (or every market's) go back to their usual over a day. It changes the economy: a builder or the owner must approve it on a hosted world.

effects.title: Finish a town project
effects.help: A town project of that kind open in the town (one the story posted, or any) is finished by hand. It changes the economy: a builder or the owner must approve it on a hosted world.

effects.title: Call off a town project
effects.sentence: The {project} project in {town} is called off
effects.help: A town project of that kind open in the town is called off, its gifts given back. It changes the economy: a builder or the owner must approve it on a hosted world.

effects.title: Revoke a deed
effects.help: The wolf's newest deed awarded by a Dungeon Master or a story in these words is struck from their fame.

effects.title: Tick a personal quest
effects.help: An objective of the wolf's live personal quest from that DM template is done.

effects.title: Stop a scene
effects.help: A scene of this story still playing ends now (scene failed follows, with its cue).

effects.title: Start the next chapter
effects.sentence: Start the chapter {story} for {audience} {list}, carrying its variables: {carry}, {when}
effects.help: Another story of the same campaign starts: the next chapter. With "when this one has ended" (the default) it waits until this story has ended in the game (finish, an ending phase), so what this one held (doors, residents, the weather) is let go first; "now" runs it beside this one. Its wolves: the same as this story's now, its own audience, or a list variable. Carrying: the story and per-wolf variables the next chapter declares with the same name and type start with this story's values; world variables are shared anyway. Only a story approved as part of a campaign may start one, and only a chapter of that campaign that is not running.

types.timer: a timer (a moment, counted in days since)

scopes.world: the world's (kept after the story, shared by every story)

variables.help: Declare every variable a version 2 story uses: a name, a type and a scope, a first value, and a label to show it under. A misspelt name is an error, not a new counter.
